item: A process that is stopped while a backup snapshot is still being written removes the snapshot as it exits
summary: Item 41 as first written (a cancel during a long snapshot leaves the directory) was inferred and is not so: a native cancel and an anyio cancel scope both end with the directory removed and the claim freed, now pinned by two whole-app tests. Measured on a real uvicorn (8 s snapshot), a FORCED exit, SIGINT twice, closed the loop with no task left, the interpreter waited for the non-daemon worker, and the process exited 0 with .oo-backup-*/snapshot.db, a plaintext copy of the corpus, in the data folder. The route now records the directories this pid made and an atexit hook removes what is still held (Python joins non-daemon threads before exit hooks); the table is pid-stamped so a forked child never removes its parent's live download. Same real-process probe after the change: removed. Five new tests, four mutants (no atexit registration, no registration in the route, no forget on release, no pid guard) each fail one. A kill (SIGKILL, power) still leaves the directory: the sweeps' case, item 40, waiting on the stream_backup edit of another lane. The lesson that stated item 41 is corrected in place.
